c74object.name: template
c74object.digest: Two-number calculator — a documented starting point for Max SDK development
c74object.description: template combines two numbers using the operation set by the op attribute. It exists to be taken apart: it is the smallest complete Max external that still demonstrates inlets, outlets, methods, a saved attribute, and a clean split between Max-facing glue code and a portable engine that knows nothing about Max.

inlet.digest: a (hot) — number, bang, or list "a b"
inlet.description: Sets the first operand and immediately computes and outputs. A bang recomputes with the current values. A two-element list sets both operands at once, then outputs.
Sets the second operand without producing output. This is the standard Max hot/cold convention: the left inlet triggers, the right inlet only stores.

outlet.description: The computed value, as a float.
All three values as a list, for unpacking downstream with unpack. Fired before the left outlet, so anything reacting to the result already has the matching operands available.

method.name: int
method.description: In the left inlet, sets a and outputs. In the right inlet, stores b without output.

method.name: float
method.description: Same as int, with a decimal value. All arithmetic is done in double precision internally.

method.name: bang
method.description: Recomputes using the current operands and operation, and fires both outlets. Useful for re-triggering after changing op.

method.name: list
method.description: Sets a from the first element and b from the second. Sent to the left inlet, it also computes and outputs.

attribute.name: op
attribute.description:
Which operation to perform: 0 = Add, 1 = Subtract, 2 = Multiply, 3 = Divide. Settable as a typed-in argument ([template @op 2]), from the Inspector, or at runtime with an op $1 message.
Division by zero is refused rather than producing infinity: the object posts a warning and outputs 0.
This attribute is saved with the patcher, so the chosen operation is restored when the patch reopens.

c74object.discussion:
The arithmetic lives in simple_math.c, a plain C file containing no Max code at all — no ext.h, no atoms, no outlets. The Max object owns an engine struct and calls into it; the engine never reaches back out. That split is the main thing this object exists to demonstrate, because it lets you test the engine without launching Max and reuse it in another object or another program entirely.
When a result is wrong you look in the engine; when an inlet misbehaves you look in the glue. The bug tells you which file it is in.
